payload.summary: scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh's timestamp regex (line 137) never matches this notebook's real heading format, silently regressing the 07-11 oldest-by-timestamp fix and producing duplicate/corrupted headings
payload.evidence: Regex is [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}(T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z)? -- requires DASHED date + colon-separated time-with-seconds. This notebook's actual, long-established heading convention is '## cycle-YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ -- ...' (compact, no dashes, no colons, no seconds, e.g. 'cycle-20260712T0537Z'). Live-tested: echo '## cycle-20260712T0537Z -- ...' | grep -oE '<the regex>' returns EMPTY. Every section in the file therefore falls to the no-timestamp fallback (sentinel 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z), making ALL sections tie -- sort -t: -k2 | head -1's tie-break then effectively picks by grep -n's original top-to-bottom order, i.e. the FIRST (newest, since this notebook is prepend-style) section -- reintroducing the exact newest-dropped-instead-of-oldest bug that FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ORDERING-ASSUMPTION (shipped 2026-07-11, commit e24e6b8b6) was supposed to have fixed. That fix's own regression test apparently only covers a DIFFERENT heading format (a trailing '· <ISO timestamp>' suffix) that doesn't match this file's real convention -- the fix was never actually exercised against real notebook content.
payload.observed_symptom: docs/agent-memory/notebooks/main.md got 2 duplicate ## headings (identical heading line appearing twice, back to back) after 2 sequential Edit calls each triggered the hook while the file was over the 200L cap -- router manually deduplicated both occurrences 2026-07-12T06:44Z, no data lost this time (both duplicates had identical content), but this is a live data-corruption bug in a hook that silently rewrites files.
payload.suggested_fix: Either (a) widen the regex to also match the compact YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ format actually in use, or (b) standardize this notebook's heading convention to match whatever format the regex expects and backfill existing headings. Also add a regression test case using this notebook's REAL heading format (not just the suffix-style format the existing test apparently covers) to scripts/agents-flow/test-notebook-auto-prune.sh, and investigate why 2 sequential hook firings on the same file produced a DUPLICATE rather than a clean single bad-drop (possible reentrancy/race in the drop-oldest loop).
payload.owner_hint: claude-manager-helper (owns this hook per its flow doc pointer)
